en: Unlike the myth that bats are blind, the Philippine fruit bat actually relies on its excellent eyesight to find ripe fruit at night.
Plants do not eat soil; they make their own food using sunlight through photosynthesis, absorbing only water and minerals from the ground.
Human blood is never blue; it is always red, but it appears blue through your skin because of how light reflects.
Ostriches do not bury their heads in the sand to hide; they simply lie low against the ground to avoid predators.
Goldfish do not have three-second memories; they can actually remember things for months and can be trained to navigate mazes.
Frogs and toads are different; frogs have smooth, moist skin and need water, while toads have dry, bumpy skin and live on land.
Humans do not use only ten percent of their brains; we use virtually every part of the brain throughout the day.
Butterflies do not taste food with their mouths; they use special sensory receptors on their feet to taste the leaves they land on.
Trees do not get their heavy mass from the soil; they actually build their wood using carbon dioxide gas from the air.
Camels do not store water in their humps; they store fat there to give them energy when desert food is scarce.
You do not lose most of your body heat through your head; heat escapes equally from any exposed skin on your body.
Cracking your knuckles does not cause arthritis; the popping sound is simply gas bubbles bursting in the lubricating fluid of your joints.
